correctness.rationale: Assuming the published Yi--Gill--Bu primitive classification and exact individual formula, the new proof establishes all quantifiers for every cutoff H and all fixed z>0. It counts each two-parameter set once, enumerates eight allowed mod-four classes, uses odd Möbius inversion to show each residue class has area/(2*pi^2) times H^2 with O(H log H) remainder, and shows m/H approaches a piecewise linear maximum uniformly. The exact polygon areas sum to 16/3 and the maximum height is 4, proving the exact 1/(24 z^2) tail for z>=1/2. The verifier uses exact rationals and independent finite-cell checks but is not substituted for the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The closest full-text preprint supplies the classification and individual mod-four formulas, but not the quantitative height asymptotic, the distribution under height sampling, the exact inverse-square tail, or the moment threshold. Older relative-spectra literature addresses attainable values, not multiplicities by height. The new quantitative facts require an additional coprime lattice-point sieve and eight explicit polygon-area calculations. Historical priority is not certified.

The closest October 2026 classification is an unindependently audited source theorem; the new derivation is conditional on it as a published mathematical premise.
The full text of the general Beck--Everett relation paper was not inspected; its abstract indicates different scope.

value.rationale: A motivated quantitative question following the new full classification: count rare primitive four-runner instances below loneliness 1/4 by a natural height and describe the distribution of their gaps. The answer gives a sharp codimension-two height coefficient and a nontrivial exact inverse-square limiting tail with an infinite-variance threshold. These population-level invariants are not the same as merely listing attainable loneliness values.
